ic_name: NFC / ISO 14443 (NXP AN10833 MIFARE family — subset)

fields.security_summary: ISO/IEC 14443 itself provides only data-integrity protection (CRC_A + CRC_B + parity for Type A frames) and structural anti-collision — not confidentiality, not authentication, and not replay protection. All cryptographic protection is layered above Layer 3 (MIFARE Classic Crypto1 stream cipher) or above Layer 4 (MIFARE DESFire 3DES / 3K-3DES / AES-128; MIFARE Plus AES-128 in SL2 / SL3; SmartMX / JCOP RSA / ECC). AN10833 explicitly notes (§ 2.4) that ATQA/SAK identification is not advisable for security-sensitive applications because newer chips with stronger crypto can re-use SAK values from older variants. The recommended secure identification path is (a) GetVersion on Layer 4 followed by (b) AES-128 mutual authentication before any application data exchange.

security_features.name: CRC_A (Type A frame)
security_features.scope: Type A standard frames + T=CL Layer 4 blocks
security_features.description: Polynomial 0x8408 reflected, init 0x6363, no final XOR. Detects bit-flip on the air interface; NOT a cryptographic MAC.

security_features.name: CRC_B (Type B frame)
security_features.scope: Type B frames + T=CL Layer 4 blocks (Type B)
security_features.description: Polynomial 0x8408 reflected, init 0xFFFF, final XOR 0xFFFF. Detects bit-flip; NOT cryptographic.

security_features.name: Odd parity per byte (Type A)
security_features.scope: Each byte on Type A wire
security_features.description: One odd-parity bit follows every 8 data bits LSB-first. Per-byte error detection at the cost of 11% wire overhead.

security_features.name: UID — Random ID (RID) variant
security_features.description: When UID0 = 0x08, UID1..UID3 are randomised at each Power-on Reset by a PICC-internal RNG. Defeats UID-based persistent tracking. Used by MIFARE DESFire EV2/EV3 in Random ID mode and by NFC-A peer devices.

security_features.name: MIFARE Classic Crypto1
security_features.scope: Sector-keyed READ / WRITE / DECREMENT / INCREMENT on MIFARE Classic 1K / 4K and Plus SL1
security_features.description: Proprietary NXP 48-bit stream cipher; broken by Nohl et al. (2008) and subsequent academic attacks. Per-sector Key A (read) and Key B (write); 6-byte keys. DO NOT use for new security designs.

security_features.name: MIFARE Plus AES-128 (SL2 / SL3)
security_features.scope: MIFARE Plus SL2 (sector AES) / SL3 (full AES + T=CL)
security_features.description: Standard AES-128 in CBC mode; per-sector key derivation; mutually-authenticated read and write.

security_features.name: MIFARE DESFire AES / 3K-3DES / 3DES
security_features.description: ISO 7816-style application + file model. EV2 supports Transaction MAC; EV3 adds Originality Signature based on NIST-P256 ECC. Recommended for new designs.

security_features.name: MIFARE Ultralight C 3DES
security_features.description: Per-tag 3DES authentication; weaker than AES but sufficient for low-value applications.

security_features.name: NTAG21x password (PWD_AUTH)
security_features.description: Set via WRITE command on configuration pages; 4-byte password + 2-byte PACK ack. Not cryptographically secure; defeats casual eavesdropping only.

security_features.name: Card Lock — MIFARE Classic / Ultralight OTP / Lock bytes
security_features.scope: MIFARE Classic sector trailers / Ultralight pages 2-3
security_features.description: Per-sector or per-page lock bits; once set, the protected memory is read-only. Used to freeze NDEF content.

security_features.name: Originality Signature (ECC NIST-P256)
security_features.scope: NTAG21x DNA / MIFARE DESFire EV3 / SmartMX
security_features.description: Factory-signed ECDSA signature over UID; verifiable with public key. Defeats UID cloning since attacker cannot forge the signature without the private key.

fields.no_base_layer_confidentiality: The base ISO 14443 protocol does NOT encrypt user data on the air interface. An attacker with an RF sniffer (e.g. Proxmark3 + suitable antenna) can capture both PCD commands and PICC responses cleartext at Layer 3. Confidentiality must come from Layer 4 application crypto (MIFARE Plus / DESFire) or from a secure element (SmartMX / JCOP).
fields.comparison_to_iso_15693_and_nfc_p2p: ISO 15693 (Vicinity Cards, also at 13.56 MHz but with deeper modulation depth and longer range) shares the same lack of base-layer confidentiality. NFC peer-to-peer (NFCIP-1 / ISO 18092) inherits the same wire-level transparency — application crypto must be added above DEP. Bluetooth-LE and Wi-Fi by contrast are encrypted at the link layer.
fields.notes: Security requirements at the AN10833 level are bounded by what the identification surface can guarantee: (a) UID is factory-OTP-unique (except RID), (b) ATQA + SAK are public and deterministic, (c) GetVersion is public and deterministic. None of these are cryptographically authenticated — any of them can be cloned or replayed by an attacker with a UID-emulating reader. Practical security therefore lives in the application layer above Layer 4 (DESFire AES auth, Plus SL3 AES auth, Originality Signature). EMVCo, ICAO (passport), and FIPS-201 (PIV) all require Layer-4 mutual authentication before any application data exchange.
